title: 1:1 - Alex and Marcus
segments: Hey Marcus, how's your week going so far?
Pretty good. A bit tiring, honestly. The on-call week last week was rough, and I'm still catching up on sleep.
I saw the page at three in the morning on Saturday. Thank you for handling that. Was it the same issue as before?
Same alert, different cause this time. The ingestion workers ran out of memory after a carrier sent a massive file. I put a size limit in as a stopgap, but we need a proper fix.
Let's make sure that gets a ticket and some real time. I don't want you absorbing this as a recurring cost. Do you want to own the fix?
I do, actually. It ties into what I want to work on anyway, which is streaming the files instead of loading them whole.
Good. Let's talk about that. How are you feeling about your current projects overall?
The webhook retry work is fine, but it's incremental. I'd love to take on something with more design in it. I've been thinking about the ingestion redesign.
That's the biggest technical piece we have this year, and I think you're ready for it. It would mean leading the design, writing the proposal, and pulling in Dmitri and Sofia where needed.
I'd be nervous about the leading part, to be honest. I've contributed to designs, but I've never been the person who drives the whole thing.
That's reasonable. I'll help. We can do weekly design check-ins, and I'll review the first draft before it goes to the wider team. The goal is that you're comfortable by the time it's presented.
That would help a lot. Would the webhook work get reassigned?
I'd hand it to Sofia's team or hold it. The ingestion redesign should be your focus for the next two months, with maybe a day a week for on-call follow-ups.
Okay. Then I'd want to write a short problem statement first, with numbers on how fast volume is growing, so we agree on what we're solving.
Perfect. Aim to have that to me by next Wednesday. It doesn't need to be polished.
Will do. Can I also ask about the senior promotion? We talked about it at the start of the year.
Yes, and I'm glad you brought it up. Honestly, you're close. The gap I see is scope, being the technical owner of something cross-team, and the ingestion redesign is exactly that.
So if the redesign goes well, that's the case for promotion?
That plus continued reliability work. I can't promise timing since it goes through calibration in January, but I'll write it up so the evidence is in place.
That's clear. Thanks for being direct about it.
Always. Now, anything bothering you on the team side? How are things with Sofia and Dmitri?
Good, mostly. One thing is code review turnaround. Pull requests sit for a day or more, and it blocks me when I'm trying to ship.
I've heard that from a couple of people. What would help? A rotation, a time box, a rule about response times?
A simple norm might be enough, like first review within four working hours. We tried it informally once and it worked until things got busy.
Let's propose it at the next team meeting and see if people agree. Would you be willing to bring it up since you raised it?
Last topic from me. Are you taking time off soon? You haven't used much of your leave this year.
I was thinking about a week at the end of November, around Thanksgiving.
Please do. I'll make sure on-call coverage is arranged. Book it soon so we can plan around it.
I'll put it in the calendar today.
Great. Thanks Marcus, I'll write up the notes from this one and share them with you.
overview: Alex and Marcus discussed Marcus's rough on-call week, caused by an ingestion worker memory failure after an oversized carrier file; Marcus will own the proper streaming fix. Alex proposed that Marcus lead the ingestion redesign over the next two months, with weekly design check-ins for support, and Marcus will write a short problem statement by next Wednesday. They covered the path to a senior promotion, which hinges on owning a cross-team technical project. Marcus raised slow code review turnaround and will propose a four-working-hour first-review norm to the team. He also plans a week off around Thanksgiving.
